review_candidates.description: About ARTC Join our team and be part of keeping the future of transport on track. ARTC is a vital link in Australia’s transport supply chain – operating and maintaining the national rail network to connect our regions, cities and ports. We help enable the safe and efficient transit of freight and passenger trains across the country, managing more than 9,600km of rail track across five states and the lands of more than 50 First Nations. About The Team When you join our Operations team, you’ll join the team who help keep trains moving safely and reliably across our 9,600km of track. Working across our East-West and North South corridors, the team is key to ensuring our rail network connects people and products with cities, ports and global markets. About The Opportunity Lead our people. Protect our structures. Keep Australia's rail network moving. Are you an experienced structural engineering professional who enjoys leading technical teams and making critical decisions that keep infrastructure safe and reliable? We are seeking an experienced Structures Performance Manager to lead ARTC's National Network Structures Asset Team, overseeing the inspection, assessment and performance of structural assets across our national rail network. This is a senior leadership opportunity where your technical expertise, sound engineering judgement and ability to lead people will play a critical role in protecting the safety, integrity and long-term performance of our infrastructure. You'll be responsible for leading a safety-critical structural inspection program, managing significant contractor relationships and ensuring structural risks are identified, assessed and effectively managed. Working closely with engineering specialists, maintenance teams, contractors and operational stakeholders, you'll influence asset management decisions, drive continuous improvement and help shape the future reliability of ARTC's structures. This role requires some interstate travel across ARTC’s national network to support and mentor team members, visit key structural assets, and engage with other stakeholders and technical service providers. Key Responsibilities In this role, you will: Lead, develop and support a national team of engineers and technical specialists, fostering accountability, collaboration and a strong safety culture. Oversee the planning, delivery and performance of the national structural inspection program, ensuring compliance with ARTC's Structures Code of Practice. Ensure bridges and other rail-related structures remain safe, reliable and fit for purpose through effective inspection, assessment and risk management. Manage annual inspection contracts completing visual and engineering inspections across the 10,500+ assets across the National Network, ensuring strong contractor performance, commercial accountability and quality outcomes. Oversee the identification, assessment, prioritisation and management of structural defects, ensuring appropriate escalation and risk controls. Review and endorse technical engineering reports, including structural inspections, load ratings, fatigue assessments and engineering investigations. Provide expert technical advice to support asset management strategies, maintenance priorities and future infrastructure investment decisions. Lead responses to emerging structural issues, coordinating technical assessments, operational controls and corrective actions. Build strong relationships with internal stakeholders, contractors and technical specialists to support effective infrastructure maintenance and asset performance. Drive improvements in inspection practices, engineering standards, technology and data to strengthen asset reliability and lifecycle management. What do we want from you? We're looking for an experienced engineering leader who combines strong technical expertise with the ability to lead people, manage competing priorities and make sound decisions in a complex, safety-critical environment. You'll bring a practical and solutions-focused approach, strong commercial awareness and the confidence to provide clear technical advice that supports safe and informed decision-making. To Be Successful, You'll Bring A degree qualification in Structural Engineering 10+ years relevant experience. Significant experience in structural engineering, including asset management, inspection and maintenance. Strong knowledge of rail infrastructure asset maintenance and structural integrity management. Demonstrated experience leading technical teams, with the ability to develop capability, drive accountability and support high performance. Proven experience managing complex inspection or maintenance programs, including contractors, budgets and commercial performance. Strong understanding of structural risk assessment, defect management, engineering standards and regulatory compliance. Sound knowledge of work health and safety principles and relevant rail safety legislation. Highly developed problem-solving and analytical skills, with the ability to make sound engineering decisions in complex operational environments. Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills, with the ability to influence decisions and provide clear technical advice. Experience developing commercially focused strategic business plans and delivering continuous improvement initiatives. Highly Regarded Qualifications in Project Management or Leadership. Experience working with railway structures, including bridges and other critical rail infrastructure. Experience managing engineering investigations and/or assessments such as load rating and fatigue assessments, finite element analysis, structural health monitoring and/or post incident investigations. Knowledge of Australian Standards, rail safeworking systems and the National Code of Practice. Experience developing asset management strategies and applying contemporary engineering and inspection technologies. What will you get from us? Talk to us about flexible working options Competitive remuneration Resources to support your health and wellbeing and development Novated leasing options, as well as discounts and support programs 24/7 Employee Assistance Program for all employees and their direct family members Our Organisation and Culture At ARTC, we’re proud to play a vital role in keeping Australia connected. Our culture is built on safety, collaboration and continuous improvement. We back our people to grow, build their capability and make a genuine impact on infrastructure that connects the nation for our customers and communities. If you’re looking for meaningful work, genuine purpose and national impact, you’ll find it at ARTC. We’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer and encourage applications from people of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander descent. A pply Now! Join the exciting future of rail today and find a career for life. As part of the application process, you’ll be required to undergo pre-employment criminal history, reference, and medical checks, including drug and alcohol testing. Applications close: Wednesday 9 December 2026. Note: ARTC reserve the right to progress applications prior to the closing date.

The Senior Project Integration Manager ensures that plans, targeting, referrals, service delivery, community engagement, monitoring, partner implementation and reporting connect across sectors and locations. The post-holder will identify and resolve gaps, duplication and missed opportunities between sectors; promote consistent implementation across IRC and partner teams; and ensure that integrated activities comply with NHF/OCHA requirements, approved proposals, budgets, technical standards and IRC policies. Strengthen coordination between outcome managers, field teams, support functions, and implementing partners so that communities can access complementary services through clear pathways and coordinated delivery. Promote common approaches to planning, geographic and community-level targeting, referrals, community feedback, monitoring, risk management and reporting. Support the Project Team Lead to maintain oversight of implementation quality, progress against targets, cross-sector dependencies, partner performance and compliance with donor requirements. Facilitate timely identification and resolution of integration barriers and support evidence-based adaptation across locations. Program Management, Technical Quality, and Strategy Coordinate the development and regular review of integrated workplans across all NHF locations Ensure sector plans are mutually reinforcing and sequenced appropriately, with clear links between facility-based, outreach, community-based and household-level interventions. Facilitate joint analysis of needs, vulnerability, service availability and access barriers to inform coherent targeting and delivery plans across sectors and locations. Promote practical integration opportunities, including referrals between health and nutrition services, WASH risk reduction at health and nutrition service points, protection-sensitive service delivery, and appropriate linkages to cash assistance. Ensure integrated activities include clear roles, timelines, geographic coverage, referral pathways, shared milestones and measurable outcomes, while preserving sector-specific technical accountability. Identify gaps, overlaps, bottlenecks and inconsistent practices across locations and agree corrective actions with the responsible Outcome Managers and partners Team Collaboration and Capacity Strengthening Foster a collaborative culture in which sector teams and partners share information, solve problems jointly and maintain a common focus on safe, accountable and high-quality outcomes for affected communities. Identify capacity-strengthening needs related to integrated planning, referrals, protection mainstreaming, accountability and donor compliance, and coordinate appropriate support with technical teams. Coordination & Field Support Convene and facilitate regular cross-sector coordination meetings with Outcome Managers, partner focal points and relevant support teams to review implementation progress, dependencies, risks and action points. Maintain a project-wide overview of integration across Northeast and Northwest locations, ensuring that lessons and workable approaches from one location are shared and adapted elsewhere. Support field teams to translate integrated plans into coordinated day-to-day implementation, including joint community engagement, harmonized schedules and coordinated service delivery where appropriate. Conduct regular field visits to IRC and partner implementation sites to assess the quality of integration, document barriers and agree practical follow-up actions. Escalate unresolved cross-sector, operational or partner issues to the Project Team Lead with clear analysis and recommendations. Partner Coordination Work closely with implementing partners to ensure their activities are integrated with IRC-led interventions and aligned with the approved project design, work plans, targeting criteria, referral mechanisms and reporting requirements. Facilitate shared planning and review sessions with partners and IRC Outcome Managers to align delivery schedules, geographic coverage, community engagement and follow-up actions. Promote consistent understanding of NHF/OCHA requirements, safeguarding, accountability, protection mainstreaming and relevant technical standards among partner teams. Monitor cross-sector coordination and integration commitments in partner workplans and support the identification and resolution of implementation gaps in collaboration with the Project Team Lead. Document partner coordination decisions, responsibilities, deadlines and action status, and ensure follow-up is completed. Quality, Standards and Donor Compliance Ensure integrated implementation remains aligned with the approved NHF/OCHA proposal, log frame, indicators, budget, workplan, donor conditions and reporting calendar. Work with Outcome Managers, Partners, and MEAL colleagues to promote adherence to relevant national guidelines, applicable humanitarian standards, sector protocols Support development and use of common integration tools, including site-level integration checklists, referral directories, joint supervision templates, action trackers and cross-sector review formats. Strong understanding of integrated programming, referral pathways, protection mainstreaming, accountability to affected people and inclusive service delivery. Experience with project work planning, results frameworks, donor compliance, monitoring, reporting, risk management and budget tracking. Strong facilitation, negotiation, communication, analytical and report-writing skills.
